subject: Compiler fails when integer(1) used in run functions called from BUGS code

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Compiler fails when integer(1) used in run functions called from BUGS code
parts:
Hi

I don't recall if this has come up before, so I'm not sure if this is a bug or a known limitation.

I want to write a nimble function to use within BUGS code at a deterministic node. This function will have as input some very large vectors of integers, so I would like to use integer(1) to save RAM. But the compiler fails unless I convert to double(1).   However, the original function does compile by itself (i.e. without the BUGS model). So it appears that the processing of the BUGS model is insisting integer vectors are double.

Attached is a stripped down example, including a copy-paste of the compiler error message. 

Best regards 
David

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Compiler fails when integer(1) used in run functions called from BUGS code
parts:
Hi David,

Indeed all numbers in the models are represented as doubles.  Someday it would be nice to generalize models in many ways, but that is the current system.

We've had some threads on this list in recent months involving the use of nimbleRcall to keep large data objects out of the model and instead access them through R, with some run-time overhead imposed.  If that is of interest and you can't find those threads, let us know.

HTH
-Perry

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: Compiler fails when integer(1) used in run functions called from BUGS code
parts:
Many thanks Perry for clarifying this point.  

It could be worth clarifying this detail with a dedicated sub-section (for visibility) in the user manual, since it is not immediately obvious that a stochastic node with a discrete distribution would be assigned to type double (for example). 

So if memory is a limiting factor, it seems the way to go would be to not put that large integer vector on a BUGS node, but instead initialise it via a setup function and handle it manually within run....

.... or just buy more RAM.

Cheers
David
